title: Finding Envelope
description: A reviewer finding as it flows through the aggregator. Verification (US2) attaches after dedup and before tiering, so a claim is checked once rather than once per reviewer that raised it.

claim.description: Null when the finding rests on judgment rather than a checkable fact. A null claim is NOT a defect and must not be penalized (FR-002). REQUIRED — must be explicitly null rather than omitted. Omission was a real bypass: with `claim` optional, a finding could carry verdict:confirmed with no claim at all and validate, defeating the FR-002 guard entirely. Found by review-plan-v2 on this PR; the original tests only covered explicit null, which is the shape the author thought of.

verdict.description: refuted => never rendered (FR-002). unverifiable/unchecked => rendered WITH a marker (FR-003). 'unchecked' means verification itself failed or timed out and must never silently render as confirmed.

verdict_detail.description: Why. For refuted, the observed value that contradicts the claim.

allOf.$comment: FR-002 third clause: a judgment finding carries no claim, so there is nothing to verify. Guarding this in the schema stops a future change from quietly dropping every design finding for failing verification it was never eligible for.
A refutation must say what refuted it. An unexplained drop is indistinguishable from a bug in the verifier.

kind.description: Drawn from the 2026-08-13 gold set, not invented. Every checkable-false finding measured was return_shape (the describeThrown recurrence), predicate_result (the AST predicate claim), or symbol_absent ('no tests exist').

method.description: 'execute' is gated on the sandboxing question (research R3 open question 2) and resolves to unverifiable until that is settled. enumerate + typecheck alone refute all three checkable-false gold-set findings, so SC-002 does not depend on execute shipping.
